university_name: Khoja Akhmet Yassawi International Kazakh-Turkish University
notes: The original search likely tried the exact article title and missed the actual Commons category, which is filed under a different transliteration: Category:Ahmet Yesevi University (confirmed via the institution's Wikidata P373 property, Q401546). That category has 14 real photographs, not just logos as the original notes assumed -- including University Gates, a Rectorat/administration building, a Library building, and several 'Kazakh-Turkish University' campus shots. I independently viewed several: (1) File:University_Gates_(5606895199).jpg (CC BY 2.0, Marcia Newton, geotagged 43°17'17.59"N 68°17'56.65"E in Turkestan) is real and correctly geolocated but is a small, dim, distant dusk shot where the actual gate structure is tiny and hard to make out behind trees and flagpoles -- too weak on its own to recommend. (2) File:Библиотека_Ахмет_Ясауи.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, Sqedes, 4752x3168) is a strong, clear, well-lit photo of the university's library building with its official circular emblem (a stylized turquoise dome/flame motif matching the real Yassawi visual identity) mounted over the entrance, and a Kazakhstan-format license plate on a parked car confirming location -- this is a genuinely acceptable candidate that the original search missed. IMPORTANT CAVEAT for whoever acts on this: I also checked File:Rectorat.jpg from the same category (matching the exact filename the automated pipeline apparently tried and failed to download due to rate-limiting) and it is very likely MIS-CATEGORIZED -- the photo shows a building with Arabic-script signage and partial Latin text reading '...RAT' (consistent with French 'Rectorat', a term used in Algeria/Morocco/Tunisia), a tour bus, and general architecture inconsistent with Turkestan, Kazakhstan. Do not use Rectorat.jpg. Net: I dispute the 'genuine gap' conclusion -- a real, well-licensed, correctly-identified candidate (the library photo) exists -- but flag that the category also contains at least one wrong-entity trap.
